output.answer: Yes. Humana has confirmed job eliminations as part of a multi-year restructuring, though it has not announced a single large, numbered mass layoff recently. Most recently, on October 27, 2026, a Humana spokesperson told WHAS11 that as the company makes staffing adjustments, "some roles may be eliminated while new roles and opportunities are created," without specifying how many jobs or which departments. Earlier, in late July 2025, CEO Jim Rechtin said Humana had notified eligible employees of an early retirement program that week to streamline costs and would contract out more shared-services work; the company also offered voluntary early retirement packages (reported July 29, 2025), and its FY2025 10-K recorded $329 million in severance and other employee-related charges tied to "workforce optimization" (vs. $25 million in 2024). No Humana WARN layoff notice has been filed since the start of 2025, and the last big numbered cut Humana formally announced was in 2010 (~1,400 net positions).
caveats: Humana has not disclosed how many positions are affected or which departments are involved in the current reorganization; the October 2026 statement confirms eliminations may occur but gives no headcount.

No Humana WARN (mass-layoff notice) filings appear since the start of 2025 per a layoff tracker, so the scale of individual reductions cannot be confirmed from public notices; WARN only covers qualifying mass layoffs.

The $329 million severance/workforce-optimization figure and associate headcounts (about 67,060 at end-2025) are from Humana's FY2025 Form 10-K as quoted by a secondary aggregator; the 10-K itself was not directly readable in full during this research, so exact filing wording should be verified before formal use.

Employee-forum reports (thelayoff.com) and individual LinkedIn posts describe reductions in force in 2025-2026 (e.g., digital, marketing, CenterWell teams), but these are unverified anecdotes, not company announcements.

passages.quote: "As we make these changes, some roles may be eliminated while new roles and opportunities are created in areas that support our future direction," spokesman Mark Taylor said. Taylor added Humana still has a large employee base in Louisville.

This week, we notified eligible employees of an early retirement program to help accelerate efforts with our operating model and to streamline cost. In the next few months, we will also be expanding our efforts to contract out additional aspects of our shared services functions.
passages.publisher: The Motley Fool (Humana Q2 2025 earnings call transcript, CEO Jim Rechtin)

passages.quote: Humana is offering a voluntary early retirement program for employees in some areas of the company if they meet specific requirements.
In 2025 the company recorded $329 million in severance and other employee related charges in connection with workforce optimization, against $25 million in 2024 and $199 million in 2023.
passages.publisher: The Layoff Club (quoting Humana's FY2025 Form 10-K)

passages.quote: Humana Inc. (NYSE: HUM) announced today that it intends to reduce its workforce on a net basis by approximately 1,400 positions, or five percent, over the course of 2010, balancing 2,500 position reductions with 1,100 additional jobs in areas of growth.

key_facts.fact: A Humana spokesperson said the company evaluates staffing needs on an ongoing basis and that as it makes changes, "some roles may be eliminated while new roles and opportunities are created in areas that support our future direction"; it did not say how many jobs or which departments could be impacted.

On the Q2 2025 earnings call (July 30, 2025), Humana CEO Jim Rechtin said: "This week, we notified eligible employees of an early retirement program to help accelerate efforts with our operating model and to streamline cost," and that Humana would expand contracting out of shared-services functions in the following months.
Humana confirmed it was offering a voluntary early retirement program for employees in some areas of the company if they meet specific requirements.

Humana's FY2025 Form 10-K recorded $329 million in severance and other employee-related charges tied to "workforce optimization" in 2025, versus $25 million in 2024 and $199 million in 2023; associate headcount was about 67,060 at end-2025 vs about 65,680 at end-2024.

No Humana WARN layoff notices have been filed since the start of 2025, and no Humana layoff round since 2022 has come with a publicly announced number of jobs (the December 2022 SeniorBridge closure in New York involved 1,005 layoffs).

The last large numbered workforce reduction Humana formally announced was in February 2010: a net reduction of approximately 1,400 positions (5%) over the course of 2010, balancing 2,500 position reductions with 1,100 new jobs.
